## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

None of the secondary literature passages in the dossier directly address this sutta; references titled *Jaṭila Sutta* in the dossier refer instead to the homonymous discourse featuring King Pasenadi and spies disguised as matted-hair ascetics found elsewhere in the canon (SN 3.11 / Ud 6.2).

 Resembling verse parallels also occur extensively in the "Brahmin" chapters of canonical verse collections, notably the Pali *Dhammapada* (Dhp 393), the Chinese *Dharmapada* (T 210.35), the Gāndhārī *Dharmapada* (G-Dhp 1–50), the Patna *Dharmapada* (P-Dhp 34–49), and the Tibetan *Udānavarga* (Uv Kg 33). The text is also cited in the paracanonical *Nettippakaraṇa* (Ne 37).

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on catalog data.*
